summary:
GeoCosmos is a web tool that finds the best places on Earth to rehearse missions to the Moon and Mars. Pick a target such as Shackleton Crater or Jezero Crater and a test purpose: rover driving, ice drilling, dust exposure, biosignature search, lava tubes or base construction. GeoCosmos then scans all ~250,000 land cells of Earth (25 km each) using NASA and ESA satellite data: slope and roughness, surface temperature and its day-night range, aridity, dust, mineralogy and frozen ground. It ranks sites with test-specific, documented weights. Terrain on Earth, Mars (MOLA) and the Moon (LOLA) is computed with the same rules, so the numbers are directly comparable.

Famous analogs are excluded from discovery and used only for validation, so the tool proposes new candidates. Every candidate shows where the analogy breaks (gravity, atmosphere, radiation) and how easy the site is to reach and set up. A printable site report and roadmap is included. We report our pre-registered validation honestly: the criterion was not met, and the site shows each known analog's rank against chance. Permanent bases need well-rehearsed crews and hardware, and choosing the right test site is the first step.
details:
GeoCosmos answers one question: "If we want to test X for target Y on the Moon or Mars, where on Earth should we go?" The user picks a Moon or Mars target and a test purpose. The tool ranks every land cell on Earth by similarity and shows the top candidates on a map. Each candidate card shows the place name, a per-parameter similarity breakdown, the "break points" (what Earth can never reproduce: gravity, atmosphere, radiation, liquid water, temperature extremes) and an ease-of-setup score (access, power, water, workforce, altitude). Each candidate can be printed as a site report with a test roadmap. A free-text scenario box ("I want to test a drill in dusty, cold, flat terrain") turns the user's words into weights.

HOW IT WORKS

- Earth grid: 250,022 land cells at 25 km, built in Google Earth Engine from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (slope, roughness at a common 500 m baseline), MODIS LST (temperature, day-night range), GPM IMERG + MODIS NDVI (aridity), MODIS AOD (dust), ASTER GED (mafic and carbonate indices), ESA CCI Permafrost (ground ice) and computed noon Sun elevation.

- Targets: Mars values come from MOLA and the Mars Climate Database; Moon values from LOLA and LRO Diviner. Terrain metrics use exactly the same rules as on Earth.

- Scoring: test-specific weights with a written rationale for each (config/test_profiles.yaml). Parameters that do not apply to a target (e.g. dust on the airless Moon) are dropped and their weight is redistributed.

- Validation: well-known analogs (Haughton, Atacama, Iceland, Svalbard, etc.) are excluded from discovery and split in advance into tuning, holdout and report sets. The success criterion (3 of 4 holdout sites in Earth's top 1%) was fixed before results. It was NOT met (0/4). We did not change the criterion. Instead, the validation page plots each site's percentile against chance and explains why, e.g. Lake Salda's carbonate strip is much smaller than a 25 km cell.

- AI, strictly constrained: Gemini only converts free-text scenarios into weights and writes short commentary from the engine's own numbers. Any comment that contains a number not present in the engine output is rejected. A keyword fallback works when Gemini is unavailable.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Analog sites are usually chosen by tradition and accessibility. GeoCosmos makes the choice transparent, reproducible and global, and it proposes new candidates rather than repeating famous ones. Showing where each analogy fails helps mission planners avoid over-trusting a test site. The ease-of-setup score and roadmap connect the science to real logistics. The tool is bilingual (English/Turkish) and has a plain-language explainer for the public.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, Earth Engine API), FastAPI (deployed on Render with Docker), React + Vite + TypeScript, Leaflet, Recharts, Tailwind CSS, GitHub Pages, GitHub Actions CI with automated tests, Google Gemini API.

CREATIVITY AND TEAM CONSIDERATIONS

- One set of rules for three worlds, so the comparison is fair.

- "Processes as well as places": dust, freeze-thaw and ice stability are included as parameters, not only terrain.

- Honesty as a feature: pre-registered validation, visible failure, break points on every card, a source label on every number.

- Scale: 25 km cells hide small features, so this limitation is documented and a 5 km fine scan is planned.
